new_statements.quote: All lexically heavy monosyllables are stressed, and most polysyllabic words exhibit a distinctly stressed syllable as measured by intensity levels. Although not phonemic, stress influences segmental realisations. For example, unstressed /ɔ/ has a tendency to get centralised and/or unrounded, bringing it very close to some realisations of /ɨ/, but always stays [ɔ] in a stressed position, e.g., in a lexical monosyllable: /mɔ³¹ˈtsʰɑ⁵⁵/ ‘sun’ → [mɔ³¹-] ~ [mʚ³¹-] … /ˈmɔ³¹/ ‘old’ → [mɔ³¹] … When it comes to grammatical particles, these often lack autonomous stress and become encliticised to the preceding lexical word

new_statements.rule_in_words: Luodie Phola is a tone language (four contrastive primary tones 55/33/31/22 plus context-bound secondary tones). Stress exists phonetically (intensity) but is not contrastive: every lexical monosyllable is stressed; a polysyllabic word carries one prominent syllable, whose position the author does not state as a rule (his stress-marked examples /mɔ³¹ˈtsʰɑ⁵⁵/ 'sun', /pʰɔ³¹ˈlɑ³³mɔ³³/ 'Phola woman' show a non-initial stressed syllable); grammatical particles are unstressed, encliticise to the preceding lexical word and reduce /ɔ ɑ/ toward [ɘ]; stressed lexical syllables and tense-voice vowels never reduce.
new_statements.exceptions: Particles may be stressed for emphasis; the verb 'come' lɑ³³ is stressed as main verb, unstressed as secondary verb; attentional deictics are always stressed and form their own intonation unit (p. ~95); fn. 10 p. 61: tone 22 is phonetically shorter and correlates with unstressed syllables, over-represented in grammatical morphemes.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonetic prominence measured by intensity in recorded speech; lexical word vs enclitic particle contrast; no rule for stress placement inside polysyllabic lexical words is given, so no fixed-position reading is licensed.
new_statements.identity_note: pula1268 'Pula Yi' is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO code [ypl], split (CR 2007-121, effective 2008-01-14) into Phola [ypg] = phol1237, Phala [ypa] = phal1256 and Alo Phola [ypo] = alop1235. The quoted source describes Luodie Phola (/lɑ³³ɬe³³/, Luodie village 罗垤, Wadie Township, Yuanjiang County, Yunnan; 23.459 N 102.285 E), i.e. phol1237 [ypg], the principal successor variety — the same village as Pelkey's LDC Phola datapoint. Any catalog entry should be filed under phol1237, not under the retired pula1268; nothing was found for Phala or Alo Phola. Note phol1237, phal1256 and alop1235 are separate targets; the thesis PDF saved here serves phol1237 directly.

sources.note: §3.1.4.4 'Stress and length' (pp. 56-58): Phola (Luodie) has four contrastive primary tones; stress is not phonemic; all lexical monosyllables are stressed, most polysyllabic words have one distinctly stressed (intensity-prominent) syllable; grammatical particles lack autonomous stress, encliticise and reduce their vowels; no positional rule stated (examples /mɔ³¹ˈtsʰɑ⁵⁵/ 'sun', /pʰɔ³¹ˈlɑ³³mɔ³³/ 'Phola woman' show non-initial stress); fn.10 p.61: tone 22 is shorter and correlates with unstressed syllables.
